definition: A wave pattern made when two waves with the same frequency, wavelength, amplitude and speed travel in opposite directions and superpose; the pattern stays in place and transfers no net energy.
A point on a standing wave where the amplitude is always zero, so the medium there never moves.
A point on a standing wave where the amplitude is largest, halfway between two neighbouring nodes.
One of the standing-wave patterns a string or air column can hold, numbered by $n$; the first harmonic has the lowest frequency. With one node end and one antinode end, only odd $n$ exist.
An older name for the frequency of the first harmonic, the lowest-frequency standing wave a string or pipe can hold; IB Physics says first harmonic instead.
